<!-- ============ ABOUT ============ -->
<section class="section" id="about">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="about-grid">
      <div>
        <span class="eyebrow">about</span>
        <h2>A local chapter of a worldwide movement</h2>
        <div class="body" style="margin-top:1.1rem">
          <p>RLadies+ is a worldwide organisation whose mission is to promote gender diversity in the R community. R is one of the most widely used languages for statistics, data science and reproducible research — and the people who use it should reflect the world it describes.</p>
          <p>In Geneva, we bring that mission home: a friendly space for R users across the region's universities, hospitals, international organisations, NGOs and industry to learn from each other, present their work, and grow — whatever their level.</p>
          <p>No prior experience is required. Curiosity is enough.</p>
          <p><b>You don't have to be a woman or from an underrepresented group to belong.</b> Our meetups are open to all genders — men included. What unites us is the shared goal, not who we are.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <aside class="card card--join" aria-label="Who we are">
        <h3>Who we are</h3>
        <p class="who"><b>A diverse, open community with one shared goal: more women and underrepresented people in R.</b></p>
        <p class="who" style="margin-top:.9rem">Whatever your gender, background or experience level, if you support that goal, you belong here.</p>
        <p class="who" style="margin-top:.9rem; color:var(--ink-70)"><span class="plus">+</span> Come to learn, present, mentor, or simply meet people — everyone is encouraged to take part.</p>
      </aside>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

        <p>Regular sessions with speakers from academia, the public sector and industry — real projects, real code, real questions.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="tile reveal">
        <div class="tag"># workshops</div>
        <h3>Hands-on workshops</h3>
        <p>Practical skills you can use the next day: the tidyverse, Shiny, Quarto, package development, statistics and visualisation.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="tile reveal">
        <div class="tag"># network</div>
        <h3>Community &amp; network</h3>

      </article>
      <article class="tile reveal">
        <div class="tag"># firsts</div>

      </article>

<!-- ============ EVIDENCE ============ -->
<section class="section evidence" id="evidence">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="section-head">
      <span class="eyebrow">evidence</span>
      <h2>Why a community like this matters</h2>
      <p>The gap in data science and statistics is not a story about ability — it is about who feels they belong, and that is something a community can change. Here is what the evidence shows.</p>
    </div>

    <p class="evi-sub">the gap is real</p>
    <div class="stat-grid">
      <div class="stat reveal">
        <div class="fig">~11%</div>
        <p>About 11% of authors of R packages are women — the people who build the tools the whole community depends on. That share has barely moved from roughly 9% in 2010.</p>
        <span class="src">Forwards · R Foundation task force, 2017</span>
      </div>
      <div class="stat reveal">
        <div class="fig">&lt; 1 in 5</div>
        <p>Fewer than one in five data scientists are women. On Kaggle, the field's largest community, women have hovered between about 16% and 22% of participants for years.</p>
        <span class="src">Kaggle surveys · peer-reviewed analysis, 2023</span>
      </div>
      <div class="stat reveal">
        <div class="fig">34% &rarr; 16%</div>
        <p>Women are about a third of scientific authors worldwide, but only ~16% of the most-cited researchers. The gap <b>widens with seniority</b> — exactly where the role models thin out.</p>
        <span class="src">Quantitative Science Studies, 2022</span>
      </div>
    </div>

    <p class="evi-sub">what actually moves the numbers</p>
    <div class="mech-grid">
      <div class="mech reveal">
        <div class="fig">100% stayed</div>
        <h3>Role models keep women in</h3>
        <p>In a randomised field experiment, first-year women in engineering given a <b>female</b> peer mentor had 100% retention in their major after one year — versus 82% with a male mentor and 89% with none. Belonging and confidence, not GPA, best predicted who stayed.</p>
        <span class="ref">Dennehy &amp; Dasgupta, 2017 · PNAS</span>
      </div>
      <div class="mech reveal">
        <div class="fig">effect persisted</div>
        <h3>And the effect lasts</h3>
        <p>Followed to graduation and a year beyond, the same women showed higher STEM-degree completion, more internships, and sustained ambition to continue. A brief early intervention, durable results.</p>
        <span class="ref">Wu, Thiem &amp; Dasgupta, 2022 · Nature Communications</span>
      </div>
      <div class="mech reveal">
        <div class="fig">more voice</div>
        <h3>Peers change participation</h3>
        <p>Women placed alongside female peers in small technical groups spoke up more, felt more motivated, and reported stronger career aspirations than those doing identical work in male-dominated groups.</p>
        <span class="ref">Dasgupta, Scircle &amp; Hunsinger, 2015 · PNAS</span>
      </div>
    </div>

    <p class="bridge">These trials isolate the exact mechanisms a chapter like ours is built to supply: <b>visible role models, a peer network, and a sense of belonging</b>. RLadies+ Geneva has not been run as a controlled trial — but the ingredients the evidence points to are precisely the ones we put in one room, every meetup. And the stakes are not only fairness: the European Commission estimates that closing the digital gender gap could add roughly <b>€260–600 billion</b> to EU GDP.</p>

    <div class="sources">
      <h4>SOURCES</h4>
      <ol>
        <li>Forwards — the R Foundation's diversity task force. About 11% of R package authors identified as women in 2017 (up from ~9% in 2010). <a href="https://forwards.github.io/data.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">forwards.github.io/data</a></li>
        <li>Kaggle, State of Data Science &amp; Machine Learning surveys — women were roughly 16–22% of respondents; and "The Data Science Gender Gap in the Kaggle Community" (Academy of Management Proceedings, 2023), reporting women as under 20% of data scientists. <a href="https://www.kaggle.com/kaggle-survey-2022" target="_blank" rel="noopener">kaggle.com</a></li>
        <li>Gender gap among highly cited researchers, 2014–2021. Quantitative Science Studies, 3(4), 1003 (2022) — women ~34% of authors globally but ~16% of the most-cited. <a href="https://direct.mit.edu/qss/article/3/4/1003/113322" target="_blank" rel="noopener">direct.mit.edu/qss</a></li>
        <li>European Commission, "Women in Digital" — the estimated €260–600 billion EU GDP gain from closing the digital gender gap. <a href="https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/women-digital" target="_blank" rel="noopener">digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu</a></li>
        <li>Dennehy, T. C., &amp; Dasgupta, N. (2017). Female peer mentors early in college increase women's retention in engineering. PNAS, 114(23), 5964–5969. <a href="https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1613117114" target="_blank" rel="noopener">doi:10.1073/pnas.1613117114</a></li>
        <li>Wu, D. J., Thiem, K. C., &amp; Dasgupta, N. (2022). Female peer mentors have lasting positive impacts beyond graduation. Nature Communications, 13, 6837. <a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-34508-x" target="_blank" rel="noopener">nature.com/articles/s41467-022-34508-x</a></li>
        <li>Dasgupta, N., Scircle, M. M., &amp; Hunsinger, M. (2015). Female peers in small work groups enhance women's motivation, participation, and career aspirations. PNAS, 112(16), 4988–4993.</li>
      </ol>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<script>
  // Mobile menu
  const toggle = document.querySelector('.nav-toggle');
  const menu = document.getElementById('menu');
  toggle.addEventListener('click', () => {
    const open = menu.classList.toggle('open');
    toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(open));
  });
  menu.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(a =>
    a.addEventListener('click', () => { menu.classList.remove('open'); toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false'); })
  );

  // Scroll reveal (respects reduced motion via CSS fallback)
  const io = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
    entries.forEach(e => { if (e.isIntersecting) { e.target.classList.add('in'); io.unobserve(e.target); } });
  }, { threshold: 0.12 });
  document.querySelectorAll('.reveal').forEach(el => io.observe(el));
</script>
